summary.headline: IKS Q2 FY27 revenue INR1,592 crore (+104% YoY, +78% QoQ, TruBridge consolidated for 82 days) with ~28% EBITDA margin; TruBridge treated as flat FY27.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 is the first full call after the TruBridge acquisition, with 82 days of TruBridge consolidated. Revenue was about INR1,592 crore and EBITDA about INR442 crore (~28%), including roughly INR25 crore of one-time acquisition/integration expenses. Legacy IKS constant-currency revenue grew a little over 13% YoY to about $101 million, and legacy IKS margins held at about 34.5-35%. Management said TruBridge is a year of stabilisation with no significant growth modelled for FY27, with synergies expected to start in the second half of Q3 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +104% YoY in INR; +78% QoQ in INR

financial_highlights.value: INR442 crore (~28%); ~INR459 crore before ESOP cost of ~INR17.5 crore

financial_highlights.change: a little over 13% YoY in USD

financial_highlights.value: ~$68 million for 82 days (run rate ~$75 million per quarter / ~$300 million per year)
INR217 crore; adjusted PAT INR273 crore (~17% of revenue)

financial_highlights.change: reported OCF lower by ~INR96 crore for TruBridge acquisition payment (non-recurring)

financial_highlights.value: INR101 crore (~$9 million interest for part-period)

segments.name: Legacy IKS (ambulatory / physician groups)
segments.commentary: Constant-currency revenue ~$101 million, +a little over 13% YoY; underlying EBITDA margin ~34.5-35%, maintained despite acquisition costs. Four wins in the quarter: a cross-sell into Augusta Health (Mayo Clinic network) and new logos White-Wilson, Evolve and UMass Memorial.

segments.name: Legacy TruBridge (rural/community hospitals, acute)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~$68 million for 82 days, against a ~$75 million quarterly run rate (~$300 million annualised). Pre-synergy EBITDA in line with the ~$68 million annual run-rate expectation; adjusted margin on the call was about 17.5% by an analyst's math, which management said understates the figure. About 2/3 is system of action and 1/3 system of record (~$100 million EHR).

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given. FY27: legacy IKS to keep growing above the ~12% industry growth in constant currency; TruBridge to be flat with no significant growth modelled for the year.
FY28: early signs of TruBridge system-of-action growth; management aspiration of 10-12% growth in the TruBridge system-of-action book from late FY28, with the EHR (system of record) book kept flat.

Synergies: management said nothing material realised yet, with the bulk ahead; restructuring of the financial health RCM operating model and G&A integration to play out from the second half of Q3 FY27.
Margin: management reiterated a return to early-to-mid 30s EBITDA margin by FY30 across both books; no FY28/FY29 margin guidance.

Long-term True North: INR3,000 crore (~$320 million) EBITDA target for FY30 and net leverage taken to near zero by end FY30. Net debt roughly INR5,280 crore; interest ~$10 million per quarter; loan has an 18-month principal moratorium, pricing SOFR+2.75% falling to SOFR+1.75% at 1.7x leverage.
ESOP: a grant to about 60-65 leaders of ~4% of equity, with ~80% tied to the FY30 EBITDA target; P&L impact from the second half of Q3 FY27, with disclosure on approval.
capex_capacity: TruBridge's three legacy IKS features (denial prediction and prevention, medical coding, clinical documentation/virtual care assistant) are to be integrated into the legacy COBOL-based TruBridge EHR and released to its customers by Q1 FY28.
Project Endeavor: a ground-up AI-native operating system for the rural and community market, launched in parallel, likely meaningful from FY29.
Two TruBridge customers have begun assessments to take the full IKS system-of-action platform.

System-of-intelligence build is task-specific: prior auth and denial prediction are in progress and coding knowledge graphs have been built. Management said a full ambulatory system-of-intelligence is about a one-year journey.
Technology spend at TruBridge to be re-optimised rather than cut.
demand_pricing: TruBridge engagement: 50+ customer meetings; management says EHR stickiness is higher than assumed and the patient-record base is 3.5-4x the ~5 million assumed at deal time.
Of 600+ TruBridge EHR hospitals, not more than ~200 use the financial health (RCM) offering, which management calls a large white space.

Top-10 client revenue fell from ~INR480 crore in Q1 to ~INR342 crore in Q2 because of a short-term project from a top-five client; management said this was replaced by other clients and that one-time projects across multiple clients are expected around calendar Q3-Q4 (e.g. HCC coding, retrospective chart review).
Pricing: outcome-based model; management expects incremental price compression as the model becomes more AI-led, which it says will be more than offset by productivity gains.
Competition: TruBridge clearing house (TruBridge RCM) is being offered in two or three new proposals; legacy clients under existing clearing-house contracts will not switch.

qa_highlights.question: Which cost levers will drive TruBridge margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited operating-cost levers from moving financial health RCM and medical coding to the global human-in-the-loop model with technology, technology spend re-optimisation, and SG&A synergies from removing public-company costs and integrating G&A (three of TruBridge's top five executives moved into the combined leadership).

qa_highlights.question: How should organic growth be modelled for legacy IKS and TruBridge?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy IKS to keep beating the ~12% industry growth; TruBridge flat through FY27, moderate growth from FY28, and 10-12% in its system-of-action book from late FY28 into FY29, with the system-of-record book kept flat.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt repayment schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a five-year facility with an 18-month principal moratorium, so repayments start around end of calendar 2027; interest is about $10 million per quarter, and the spread steps down from SOFR+2.75% to SOFR+1.75% at 1.7x leverage.

qa_highlights.question: When does the ESOP performance-linked charge hit P&L and what immediate synergies were realised?
qa_highlights.answer: The ESOP charge starts in the second half of Q3 FY27 once approved. Management said no material synergies were realised in the 82 days, with the bulk ahead, and the near-term triggers are RCM operating-model restructuring and G&A integration from the second half of Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Can IKS products be cross-sold into TruBridge's base, and vice versa?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not cross-sell the TruBridge EHR into the legacy IKS physician base; instead, TruBridge's acute RCM and its Encoder coding tool are to be sold into the IKS base.

qa_highlights.question: Is the system of intelligence commercially ready?
qa_highlights.answer: It is being built by task. Coding knowledge graphs exist, and prior auth and denial prediction are in development; a complete ambulatory system of intelligence is about a one-year journey.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI productivity being passed on to clients as price compression?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the outcome-based model keeps most productivity gains in margin, and it expects incremental price compression as the model becomes more AI-led, which it expects to be more than offset.

risks_watch: TruBridge client churn in the financial health base, which management says is being stabilised and is flat in FY27.
Synergy delivery: whether the second-half FY27 restructuring of the RCM operating model and G&A integration deliver margin gains toward early-to-mid 30s by FY30.
Lumpiness of one-time revenue projects (calendar Q3-Q4) and the top-10 client revenue decline (INR480 crore to INR342 crore QoQ).
Execution risk: Q1 FY28 target for the three features in the legacy COBOL TruBridge EHR, and Project Endeavor timelines.
Price compression as AI automation increases, and competition for clearing-house and RCM deals.
ESOP grant (~4% of equity) dilution and its effect on adjusted EBITDA, plus leverage reduction versus the INR3,000 crore FY30 EBITDA target.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the TruBridge integration, EHR stickiness and the long-term AI strategy, but explicitly non-committal on numbers ("not giving guidance at all"). Management was evasive on the TruBridge margin split, deferring it to an offline call, and on the client-level detail behind the top-10 revenue drop.
key_quotes: I am happy to report that we are able to maintain those margins in spite of significant acquisition expenses, of which there were about nearly INR25 crores of acquisition expenses in this quarter.
I wouldn't model too much growth, at least for FY 2028 and FY 2029, in the TruBridge system of record business, because the idea is that's the platinum mine.
If I were you, I would not be modeling any significant growth in the TruBridge business this fiscal year.
The bulk of the synergies lie ahead of us. That is by design.

adds.what: TruBridge EHR features (denial prediction, medical coding, clinical documentation) integrated into legacy COBOL-based EHR, released to customers by Q1 FY28
Project Endeavor AI-native operating system for rural/community market, likely meaningful from FY29

growth.why: Legacy IKS guided to grow above ~12% industry growth in constant currency (Q2 was a little over 13%), while TruBridge is modelled flat for FY27 with synergies only from H2 Q3 FY27; the 104% YoY reported revenue jump is mostly acquisition consolidation, and the forward growth case rests on vague demand, cross-sell and synergy commentary rather than specific capacity or contracts.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management reiterated early-to-mid 30s EBITDA margin by FY30 across both books, with synergies from RCM restructuring and G&A integration starting H2 Q3 FY27, though legacy IKS margin is ~34.5-35% and blended Q2 EBITDA is ~28% including ~INR25 crore one-time costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or branches discussed; the only build is software features (TruBridge EHR add-ons by Q1 FY28) and TruBridge utilisation is not quantified, so no physical capacity signal.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Legacy IKS constant-currency revenue grew a little over 13% YoY to ~$101 million and management guided to keep beating the ~12% industry growth, while TruBridge is modelled flat for FY27 at ~$75 million quarterly run rate.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed and utilisation was not disclosed; the company is an asset-light services business with no utilisation metric given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No formal guidance is given; TruBridge is modelled flat for FY27 and management is explicitly non-committal on numbers, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Top-10 client revenue fell from ~INR480 crore in Q1 to ~INR342 crore in Q2 (about -29% QoQ), and synergies are not yet realised, so the flat TruBridge case and margin path carry execution risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: TruBridge EHR add-ons (denial prediction, medical coding, clinical documentation) are to be released to customers by Q1 FY28, and two TruBridge customers have started assessments for the full IKS system-of-action platform.

rows.label: Outcome-based pricing with AI-led price compression
rows.why: Management expects incremental price compression as the model becomes more AI-led, which it says will be more than offset by productivity gains, so margin benefit depends on that offset.

rows.label: One-time TruBridge projects in calendar Q3-Q4
rows.why: Management expects one-time projects across multiple clients (HCC coding, retrospective chart review) around calendar Q3-Q4, after Top-10 client revenue fell from ~INR480 crore to ~INR342 crore QoQ.

rows.label: TruBridge RCM restructuring and G&A integration synergies
rows.why: Synergies start from the second half of Q3 FY27 via moving financial health RCM and coding to a global human-in-the-loop model, with nothing material realised in the 82 days so far.

tone.note: Management was confident on TruBridge EHR stickiness, the AI strategy and legacy IKS growth above 12%, but non-committal on numbers and evasive on the TruBridge margin split and top-10 client detail; analysts pushed on margins and revenue lumpiness.
